Passage IV
Water that flows through underground aquifers (layers
of permeable rock that serve as underground reservoirs)
sometimes contains undesirable amounts of the elements
arsenic (As) and antimony (Sb). Scientists studied how the
amounts of As and Sb in groundwater from 2 coastal plain
aquifers (Aquifers 1 and 2) varied along their known
groundwater flow paths. The aquifers were unrelated.
Study
Aquifer 1 consisted of carbonate rock layers, while
Aquifer 2 consisted of unconsolidated quartz sand. Within
each aquifer, groundwater samples were taken from
existing wells along known flow paths at various distances
from the aquifer’s recharge zone (area where precipitation
and surface runoff enters the underground aquifer). For
Aquifer 1, 11 wells were sampled; for Aquifer 2, 6 wells
were sampled. Prior to sample collection, all collection
containers were rigorously cleaned. For each well, a
500 mL sample of groundwater was collected and
immediately passed through a filter into its own sample
bottle. A 60 mL portion of the filtered sample was then
removed and analyzed for As and Sb. As and Sb contents
were both measured in nanomoles per kilogram (nmol/kg).
The results for Aquifer 1 are shown in Figures 1 and
2, and the results for Aquifer 2 are shown in Figures 3
and 4.
